beats.say: Two ages today: 47 for Arjun and 9 for Riya. The question takes us back 6 years and asks for the gap between them.
The word ago means we go back in time, so both ages get smaller. 6 years ago Arjun was 47 minus 6, which is 41.
Riya was 6 years younger too. 9 minus 6 is 3.
So back then they were 41 and 3. What is the gap between those two ages?

ask.ifNot: For a gap, take the smaller age away from the bigger one: 41 minus 3.

beats.say: 41 minus 3 is 38. The difference 6 years ago was 38 years.
Now look at today's ages. 47 minus 9 is also 38. The very same gap!
That is no accident. Both of them grew older by the same 6 years, so the gap between them did not change.
Next time you can go straight there. The difference in ages never changes, so just subtract today's ages. The answer is 38.
Two ages today: 27 for Arjun and 28 for Riya. The question jumps 10 years ahead and asks what the ages add up to then.
The word after means we go forward in time, so ages go up. After 10 years Arjun will be 27 plus 10, which is 37.
Now Riya. What do we do with Riya's age?

ask.ifNot: Time passes for everybody. Riya also grows 10 years older, so we add 10 to 28 as well.

beats.say: Riya grows older as well. 28 plus 10 is 38.
Now we add the two new ages. 37 plus 38 is 75.
So after 10 years, their ages will add up to 75.
Here is a quick check. Today they add up to 55. Each of them gains 10 years, so we add 10 twice. We reach 75 again.
So when time passes, everyone in the sum grows older. Two people means the years are added twice.
Two ages today: 40 for Siya and 34 for Aditya. The question takes us back 10 years and asks for the gap between them.
The word ago means we go back in time, so both ages get smaller. 10 years ago Siya was 40 minus 10, which is 30.
Aditya was 10 years younger too. 34 minus 10 is 24.
So back then they were 30 and 24. What is the gap between those two ages?

ask.ifNot: For a gap, take the smaller age away from the bigger one: 30 minus 24.

beats.say: 30 minus 24 is 6. The difference 10 years ago was 6 years.
Now look at today's ages. 40 minus 34 is also 6. The very same gap!
Here is why. Every birthday adds 1 year to both of them, so the gap between two ages never changes.
Next time you can go straight there. The difference in ages never changes, so just subtract today's ages. The answer is 6.
Riya is 26 and Rohan is 11. We want the difference in their ages, but 3 years ago.
The word ago means we go back in time, so both ages get smaller. 3 years ago Riya was 26 minus 3, which is 23.
Rohan was 3 years younger too. 11 minus 3 is 8.
So back then they were 23 and 8. What is the gap between those two ages?

ask.ifNot: For a gap, take the smaller age away from the bigger one: 23 minus 8.

beats.say: 23 minus 8 is 15. The difference 3 years ago was 15 years.
Now look at today's ages. 26 minus 11 is also 15. The very same gap!
Here is why. Every birthday adds 1 year to both of them, so the gap between two ages never changes.
So remember: the gap between two people's ages stays the same, in the past, today and for ever. Here it is 15.
Two ages today: 35 for Tara and 31 for Dev. The question jumps 4 years ahead and asks what the ages add up to then.
The word after means we go forward in time, so ages go up. After 4 years Tara will be 35 plus 4, which is 39.
Now Dev. What do we do with Dev's age?

ask.ifNot: Time passes for everybody. Dev also grows 4 years older, so we add 4 to 31 as well.

beats.say: Dev grows older as well. 31 plus 4 is 35.
Now we add the two new ages. 39 plus 35 is 74.
So after 4 years, their ages will add up to 74.
Here is a quick check. Today they add up to 66. Each of them gains 4 years, so we add 4 twice. We reach 74 again.
So when time passes, everyone in the sum grows older. Two people means the years are added twice.
5 years ago, a mother's age and her daughter's age added up to 5 x. We want what they will add up to 5 years from now.
Do not worry about the 5 x. It is just a name for a number we are not told. All we need is how much the sum grows.
From 5 years ago to 5 years from now. How many years is that?

ask.ifNot: From 5 years ago up to today is 5 years. From today to 5 years ahead is 5 more. So 5 plus 5.

beats.say: 5 plus 5 is 10. So 10 years go by.
Now the trap. In those 10 years, how much does the sum of the two ages grow?

ask.ifNot: The mother grows 10 years older. The daughter grows 10 years older too. Two people, so 10 and 10 more.

beats.say: 10 for the mother and 10 for the daughter. 10 plus 10 is 20. The sum grows by 20.
The sum was 5 x. Now it is 20 bigger. So the answer is 5 x plus 20.
Let us test it with real ages. Say they were 30 and 5 back then, which adds up to 35. Ten years on they are 40 and 15, which adds up to 55. And 55 is 35 plus 20.
When time passes, every person in the sum grows older. Two people, 10 years each, makes 20 more. So it is 5 x plus 20.
6 years ago, a husband's and wife's ages added up to 48. Today the husband, wife and son add up to 63. How old will the son be 6 years from now?
Three different times are mixed up here: 6 years ago, now, and 6 years from now. Let us bring everything to now first.
6 years ago the husband and wife added up to 48. What do the two of them add up to now?

ask.ifNot: The husband is 6 years older now, and the wife is 6 years older too. So add 6 twice.

beats.say: 48, plus 6 for the husband, plus 6 for the wife. That is 60. This is the trap: two people, so we add 6 twice.
Now all three add up to 63. Take away the parents' 60 and the son is left. 63 minus 60 is 3. The son is 3 years old now.
Is 3 our answer?

ask.ifNot: Read the last line again. It asks for the son's age 6 years from now, not his age today.

beats.say: 6 years from now he will be 3 plus 6, which is 9. So the son will be 9 years old.

board.text: The son will be 9 years old

beats.say: So bring every sum to the same time first. And when time moves, add the years once for each person.
3 years ago, the ages of Nirav and Vipul added up to 38. Vipul is 2 years younger than Nirav. We want Vipul's age after 2 years.

board.text: Vipul is 2 years younger than Nirav

beats.say: First bring the sum to today. 3 years ago they added up to 38. What do their ages add up to now?

ask.ifNot: Nirav is 3 years older now, and Vipul is 3 years older too. So add 3 twice.

beats.say: 38 plus 3 plus 3 is 44. Two people, so the 3 is added twice.
Now we split the 44 between them. Look at the bars. Nirav's bar is the same as Vipul's bar, plus 2 extra years.
Take away Nirav's 2 extra years. 44 minus 2 is 42. Now we have two equal bars.
Half of 42 is 21. So Vipul is 21 years old now.
The question asks for Vipul's age after 2 years. So what do we do?

ask.ifNot: After means going forward in time. Vipul will be 2 years older than he is now.

beats.say: 21 plus 2 is 23. So after 2 years Vipul will be 23 years old.
Check today's ages. Vipul is 21, so Nirav is 2 more, which is 23. And 21 plus 23 is 44. It fits.
So: bring the sum to today, take away the extra years, halve, and then move to the time the question asks about.
Asha is 9 years old now. We want her age after 6 years.
After 6 years. Are we moving forward in time, or back?

ask.ifNot: After means later on, in the future. As the years go by, Asha grows older.

beats.say: Every birthday adds 1 to her age. 6 birthdays add 6. So we add: 9 plus 6. Count on 6 from 9: 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15.
So Asha will be 15 years old.
Two slips to watch for. 9 minus 6 would be her age 6 years ago. And 9 times 6 is far too big: each year adds only 1.
Check: 15 minus 6 takes us back to 9, her age now.
The word after means forward in time, so add the years.
Meera is 10 years old and her father is 38. How many years older than Meera is her father?

board.text: How many years older is her father?

beats.say: How many years older. Those words ask for the gap between the two ages.
How do we find the gap between two numbers?

ask.ifNot: Adding would put the two ages together. For how much older, take the smaller age away from the bigger one.

beats.say: 38 minus 10. Take one ten away from 38 and we have 28.
So her father is 28 years older than Meera.
Check: start at Meera's age, 10, and add 28. We land on 38, her father's age.
Here is a nice fact. When Meera was born, her father was 28. And he will always be 28 years older than her.
So the words how much older mean: subtract the smaller age from the bigger one.
Tina is 8 years old. Her mother is 4 times as old as Tina. How old is her mother?

board.text: Her mother is 4 times as old. Mother = ?

beats.say: 4 times as old. Picture Tina's age as one block of 8. Her mother's age is 4 of those blocks.
So which sum gives the mother's age?

ask.ifNot: The words times as old tell us to multiply. 8 plus 4 would make her only 4 years older than Tina.

beats.say: 8 times 4. Count four 8s: 8, 16, 24, 32.
So her mother is 32 years old.
Does it make sense? A mother is much older than her 8 year old child, and 32 sounds right.
Remember: times as old means multiply.
Four years ago, Zoya was 6 years old. How old is she now?
Four years ago is in the past. To come back to today, does her age go up or down?

ask.ifNot: She was 6 back then. Since then she has had 4 more birthdays, so she is older today.

beats.say: From then to now, 4 years have passed. So we add 4. 6 plus 4 is 10.
So Zoya is 10 years old now.
The trap is to see the word ago and subtract. But the 6 is already her age in the past. Coming forward to today, we add.
Check: go back 4 years from 10 and we get 6, just as the question says.
So first ask where you are on the timeline. From the past up to now, add.
Dev was born in the year 2015. How old was he on his birthday in 2024?

board.text: His age on his birthday in 2024 = ?

beats.say: On each birthday Dev's age goes up by 1. So his age is the number of years from 2015 to 2024.
How do we find the number of years from 2015 to 2024?

ask.ifNot: The years between two dates come from subtracting the earlier year from the later one.

beats.say: 2024 minus 2015 is 9. You can count the hops on the line too: 9 hops take you from 2015 to 2024.
So Dev was 9 years old.
The trap is counting 2015 itself as year 1. But in 2015 Dev was a newborn baby, 0 years old. His first birthday came in 2016.
So age on a birthday is that year minus the birth year.
Rohan's father is 36 years old. Rohan is one-third as old as his father. How old is Rohan?

board.text: Rohan is one-third as old. Rohan = ?

beats.say: One-third means: cut the father's age into 3 equal parts, and take 1 of them.
So what do we do with 36?

ask.ifNot: Cutting into 3 equal parts is dividing by 3. Rohan is younger than his father, so the answer must be smaller than 36.

beats.say: 36 divided by 3 is 12, because 3 times 12 is 36.
So Rohan is 12 years old.
Careful: one-third is not the same as half. Half of 36 would be 18. A third means 3 equal parts, so each part is smaller.

board.text: Half of 36 is 18: not what we want

beats.say: So one-third as old means divide by 3.
Anil is 3 years older than his brother Sunil today. How many years older will Anil be after 10 years?

board.text: Anil is 3 years older than Sunil today
After 10 years, how many years older is Anil?

beats.say: No ages are given, so let us try some. Say Sunil is 5 today. Then Anil is 5 plus 3, which is 8.
Now jump 10 years ahead. Sunil will be 15 and Anil will be 18.
So after 10 years, how many years older is Anil?

ask.ifNot: Take Sunil's new age away from Anil's new age: 18 minus 15.

beats.say: 18 minus 15 is 3. Still 3 years older!
That is no accident. Both brothers grow older by the same 10 years. So the gap between them stays exactly the same.
So Anil will still be 3 years older.

board.text: Anil will still be 3 years older

beats.say: The gap between two people's ages never changes. Not after 10 years, not ever.
Ravi is 12 years old now. In how many years will he be 20?

board.text: In how many years will he be 20?

beats.say: We know his age now, 12, and his age later, 20. We want the number of years in between.
How do we find the years in between?

ask.ifNot: Adding 20 and 12 would join the two ages together. For the years in between, take the age now away from the age later.

beats.say: 20 minus 12 is 8. You can also count on from 12 until you reach 20. That takes 8 hops.
So Ravi will be 20 in 8 years.
Check: 12 plus 8 is 20. Yes.
So the age later, minus the age now, gives the years in between.
Amit is 3 years older than Bina. Bina is 2 years older than Chirag. Chirag is 7. How old is Amit?

board.text: Amit is 3 years older than Bina
Bina is 2 years older than Chirag

beats.say: This is a chain of three children. Which child's age do we know for sure?

ask.ifNot: Only one age is given as a number: Chirag is 7. So the chain starts with Chirag.

beats.say: Start with Chirag, who is 7. Bina is 2 years older than Chirag. So Bina is 7 plus 2, which is 9.
Next link. Amit is 3 years older than Bina. Careful: older than Bina, not older than Chirag.
9 plus 3 is 12.
So Amit is 12 years old.
Check the order: Chirag 7, Bina 9, Amit 12. Each one is older than the one before, just as the question says.
So start from the age you know and walk along the chain, one person at a time.
Farhan is 11 years old. His sister Rehana is 3 years younger. How old was Rehana 2 years ago?

board.text: Farhan is 11. Rehana is 3 years younger.
How old was Rehana 2 years ago?

beats.say: There are two steps here. First Rehana's age now. Then we go back 2 years.
Rehana is 3 years younger than Farhan. So how old is she now?

ask.ifNot: Younger means a smaller age. So take 3 away from Farhan's 11.

beats.say: 11 minus 3 is 8. Rehana is 8 now.
But the question asks about 2 years ago. Ago means back in time, so her age was smaller. 8 minus 2 is 6.
So Rehana was 6 years old.
Careful not to stop at 8. That is her age now. And 8 plus 2 would be her age two years from now, not two years ago.
So find the age now first, then move along the timeline: back for ago, forward for after.
Diya is 7 and her mother is 35. After 7 years, how many times as old as Diya will her mother be?

board.text: After 7 years, mother = ? times Diya's age

beats.say: Today her mother is 5 times as old, because 5 times 7 is 35. But be careful: that will not stay true. After 7 years both ages change.
After 7 years Diya will be 7 plus 7, which is 14. Her mother will be 35 plus 7, which is 42.
How do we find how many times as old the mother is?

ask.ifNot: 42 minus 14 gives the gap in years. The words how many times ask how many 14s fit into 42, and that is dividing.

beats.say: 14 times 3 is 42. So 42 divided by 14 is 3.
So her mother will be 3 times as old as Diya.

board.text: Her mother will be 3 times as old

beats.say: Notice what happened. The gap stays at 28 years for ever. But the number of times changed, from 5 times down to 3 times.
So for how many times as old at a later date: find both new ages first, then divide.
The ages of Anu and her mother add up to 44 years. Anu is 8. How old was her mother when Anu was born?

board.text: Anu + her mother = 44 years. Anu is 8.
Mother's age when Anu was born = ?

beats.say: First the mother's age now. Together they are 44, and Anu is 8. So her mother is 44 minus 8, which is 36.
Now go back to the day Anu was born. How many years ago was that?

ask.ifNot: Anu is 8 years old. So she was born 8 years ago.

beats.say: Anu was born 8 years ago. Her mother was 8 years younger then. 36 minus 8 is 28.
So her mother was 28 years old when Anu was born.
Careful: 36 is her mother's age today. We had to take 8 away twice: once to split the sum, and once to go back in time.
Check: when Anu was 0, her mother was 28. Today they are 8 and 36, and 8 plus 36 is 44. It fits.
So find the age now, then go back by the child's age to reach the day the child was born.
The ages of two sisters add up to 20 years. One is 4 years older than the other. How old is the older sister?

board.text: Two sisters' ages add up to 20
One is 4 years older. The older sister = ?

beats.say: Look at the bars. The older sister's bar is the same as the younger one's, plus 4 extra years.
If we take away those 4 extra years, what is left of the 20?

ask.ifNot: Taking away means subtracting. 20 minus 4 is 16.

beats.say: 20 minus 4 is 16. Now the two bars are equal, and together they make 16.
Half of 16 is 8. So the younger sister is 8.
The older sister gets her 4 years back. 8 plus 4 is 12. So the older sister is 12.

board.text: The older sister is 12 years old

beats.say: Check: 8 plus 12 is 20, and 12 is 4 more than 8. Both clues fit.
The trap is to halve the 20 straight away. That would make the sisters the same age, and one is older.
So: take away the extra, halve, then add the extra back for the older one.
A father is 3 times as old as his son. Their ages add up to 48 years. How old is the son?

board.text: A father is 3 times as old as his son
Their ages add up to 48. The son = ?

beats.say: Think of the son's age as 1 block. The father is 3 times as old, so he is 3 of the same blocks.
How many equal blocks are there altogether?

ask.ifNot: Count the son's own block too. 1 block for the son, and 3 for the father.

beats.say: 1 plus 3 is 4 blocks. This is the trap: do not forget the son's own block.
The 4 blocks add up to 48. So one block is 48 divided by 4, which is 12.
The son is one block. So the son is 12 years old.
Check: the father is 3 times 12, which is 36. And 12 plus 36 is 48. It fits.
So when one age is so many times another, draw blocks, count them all, and share the total.
Three years ago, Kiran was 9 years old. How old will she be 4 years from now?

board.text: How old will she be 4 years from now?

beats.say: There are two jumps on the timeline: from the past up to today, and then from today into the future.
First jump. She was 9 three years ago. So how old is she today?

ask.ifNot: From three years ago up to today, 3 years have passed. She is older now: 9 plus 3.

beats.say: 9 plus 3 is 12. Kiran is 12 today.
Second jump: 4 years from now. 12 plus 4 is 16.
So Kiran will be 16 years old.
The trap is to add the 4 straight to the 9. That skips the 3 years that have already gone by.
A quick check: from three years ago to four years ahead is 7 years in all. And 9 plus 7 is 16.
So always find today's age first, then jump to the time the question asks about.
The ages of Geeta and Hari add up to 25 years now. What did their ages add up to 3 years ago?

board.text: What did their ages add up to 3 years ago?

beats.say: Three years ago. So we go back in time, and the ages were smaller.
How many people were 3 years younger back then?

ask.ifNot: Time goes back for everybody. Geeta was 3 years younger, and Hari was 3 years younger too.

beats.say: Geeta was 3 years younger, and so was Hari. 3 plus 3 is 6. So the sum was 6 years smaller.
25 minus 6 is 19. So three years ago their ages added up to 19 years.

board.text: Their ages added up to 19 years

beats.say: The trap is to take away 3 only once. The sum has two people in it, so the 3 comes off twice.
Let us test it with real ages. Say Geeta is 12 and Hari is 13 now. Three years ago they were 9 and 10, which adds up to 19.
So when a sum of ages moves in time, it moves once for every person in it.
Jay's grandfather is 72. Jay's father is half as old as the grandfather. Jay is one-quarter as old as his father. How old is Jay?

board.text: Grandfather is 72. Father is half as old.
Jay is one-quarter as old as his father. Jay = ?

beats.say: We work down the family, one step at a time. First the father. Half of 72 is 36. So the father is 36.
Jay is one-quarter as old as his father. So we take one-quarter of which number?

ask.ifNot: Read it again: one-quarter as old as his father. The father is 36, so we take a quarter of 36, not of the grandfather's 72.

beats.say: One-quarter means 4 equal parts. So divide 36 by 4. 36 divided by 4 is 9.
So Jay is 9 years old.
Check by climbing back up the family. 9 times 4 is 36, the father. And 36 times 2 is 72, the grandfather.
So use each age to find the next one. Half means divide by 2. One-quarter means divide by 4.
Varun is 9 years old. His father is 27 years older than him. How old will his father be when Varun is 15?

board.text: Varun is 9. His father is 27 years older.

beats.say: Here is the key fact about ages. The gap between two people never changes. The father is 27 years older today, and he always will be.
So when Varun is 15, how do we find his father's age?

ask.ifNot: At that time Varun is 15, and his father is still 27 years older than him. So add 27 to 15.

beats.say: 15 plus 27. First 15 plus 20 is 35. Then 7 more is 42.
So his father will be 42 years old.

board.text: His father will be 42 years old

beats.say: Here is another way. The father is 9 plus 27, which is 36 now. Varun reaches 15 in 6 years, and 36 plus 6 is 42. The same answer.
Careful: 36 is the father's age now. The question asks for his age later, when Varun is 15.
So remember: the gap between two ages stays the same for ever. Use it at any time you like.
Rahul is 10 and his father is 40. After how many years will the father be 3 times as old as Rahul?

board.text: After ? years, father = 3 times Rahul's age

beats.say: Today the father is 4 times as old, since 4 times 10 is 40. As the years pass, both ages go up together, and that number of times gets smaller.
One thing never changes: the gap. 40 minus 10 is 30. The father is always 30 years older.
When the father is 3 times as old, picture Rahul as 1 block and his father as 3 blocks. The father's 2 extra blocks are the gap.
The 2 extra blocks make 30 years. So how big is 1 block?

ask.ifNot: 2 blocks are 30 years. So one block is half of 30.

beats.say: 30 divided by 2 is 15. One block is Rahul's age at that time. So Rahul will be 15.
Rahul is 10 now. He will be 15 after 15 minus 10, which is 5 years.
Check: after 5 years the father is 45. And 3 times 15 is 45. It works.
You could also test a choice. After 10 years they would be 20 and 50. But 3 times 20 is 60, not 50. So 10 years is too late.
So use the gap. It never changes, and here it is 2 blocks. The answer is after 5 years.
Ali is 14 and his sister Sara is 8. How old was Ali when Sara was exactly half his age?

board.text: Ali is 14. His sister Sara is 8.
Ali's age when Sara was half his age = ?

beats.say: Start with the gap. 14 minus 8 is 6. Ali is always 6 years older than Sara.
When Sara is half of Ali's age, Sara is 1 block and Ali is 2 blocks. So Ali's extra block, the gap, is the same size as Sara's age.
The gap is 6 years. So how old was Sara at that time?

ask.ifNot: Sara's block and the gap block are the same size. The gap is 6, so Sara was 6.

beats.say: Sara was 6. Ali was 6 years older: 6 plus 6 is 12.
So Ali was 12 years old.
Check: half of 12 is 6. Yes, Sara was exactly half of Ali's age.
Two traps. 6 was Sara's age, but the question asks for Ali. And half of 14 is 7, but when Ali was 7, Sara was only 1.
So when one person is double the other, the younger one's age is equal to the gap.
Five years ago, a mother was 7 times as old as her daughter. The mother is 33 now. How old is the daughter now?

board.text: Five years ago: mother = 7 times daughter

beats.say: The 7 times clue is about five years ago. So we must go back to that time before we use it. That is the trap: do not divide 33 by 7.
Five years ago the mother was 33 minus 5, which is 28.
Back then she was 7 times as old as her daughter. So how old was the daughter then?

ask.ifNot: The mother's age was 7 times the daughter's. So the daughter's age is the mother's 28 shared into 7 equal parts.

beats.say: 28 divided by 7 is 4. The daughter was 4 years old then.
Now come back to today. 5 years have passed, so the daughter is 4 plus 5, which is 9.
So the daughter is 9 years old now.

board.text: The daughter is 9 years old now

beats.say: Careful to add the 5 years just once, and only at the end. 4 was her age back then. 9 is her age now.
So go to the time the clue talks about, do the sum there, then come back to today.
Aman is twice as old as Bhavna. Four years ago, Aman was three times as old as Bhavna was then. How old is Bhavna now?

board.text: Aman is twice as old as Bhavna
4 years ago, Aman was 3 times as old as Bhavna

beats.say: Two clues, and both must be true. A good plan: try an age for Bhavna, use the first clue to get Aman's age, then test the second clue.
Try Bhavna as 12. Then Aman is twice that, which is 24. Four years ago they were 8 and 20.
Four years ago Aman should be 3 times as old as Bhavna. Is 20 equal to 3 times 8?

ask.ifNot: 3 times 8 is 24. But Aman was 20 then, so the second clue does not fit.

beats.say: So 12 does not work. Cross it out, and let us try a smaller age: 8.
If Bhavna is 8, Aman is twice that, which is 16. Four years ago they were 4 and 12.
And 3 times 4 is 12. Yes! This time both clues fit.
So Bhavna is 8 years old now.
Mind the traps. 16 is Aman's age. And 4 was Bhavna's age four years ago. The question asks for Bhavna now.
When two clues must both be true, try an age, and test it against every clue.
A grandfather is 9 times as old as his grandson. Their ages add up to 70. How old will the grandfather be when the grandson is 10?

board.text: Grandfather is 9 times as old as his grandson
Grandfather's age when the grandson is 10 = ?

beats.say: The grandson is 1 block and the grandfather is 9 blocks. Together that is 10 blocks.
10 blocks make 70, so one block is 7. The grandson is 7 now, and the grandfather is 9 times 7, which is 63.
The grandson is 7 now. In how many years will he be 10?

ask.ifNot: From 7 up to 10 is 3 steps: 8, 9, 10. So 3 years.

beats.say: 10 minus 7 is 3. So we move 3 years ahead.
Now the trap. Do we multiply by 9 again? We do not. He is 9 times as old only today. Later on, both of them simply grow 3 years older.
63 plus 3 is 66. So the grandfather will be 66 years old.

board.text: The grandfather will be 66 years old

beats.say: So find both ages now, using blocks. Then move both people forward by the same number of years.
Neel says that in 6 years he will be twice as old as he was 2 years ago. How old is Neel now?

board.text: In 6 years, Neel will be twice as old
as he was 2 years ago. Neel now = ?

beats.say: There are two moments: 2 years ago, and 6 years from now. At the later moment he is twice as old. So the earlier age is 1 block, and the later age is 2 blocks.
How many years are there from 2 years ago to 6 years from now?

ask.ifNot: From 2 years ago up to today is 2 years. From today onwards is 6 more. So 2 plus 6.

beats.say: 2 plus 6 is 8 years. In those 8 years his age grows by exactly one block. So one block is 8.
That means 2 years ago Neel was 8.
Come forward 2 years to today. 8 plus 2 is 10. So Neel is 10 now.
Check: in 6 years he will be 16. And twice 8 is 16. It works.
Careful: 8 was his age 2 years ago, and 16 will be his age in 6 years. Today he is 10.
So mark the two moments, count the years between them, and ask what that stretch of time must equal.
Three sisters were born 2 years apart, one after another. Their ages add up to 27. How old is the youngest?

board.text: Their ages add up to 27. Youngest = ?

beats.say: Picture the three ages in a row. The youngest is 2 below the middle sister. The oldest is 2 above her. So the middle sister's age is the fair share.
If the 27 years are shared equally among the three, what does each get?

ask.ifNot: Sharing equally among 3 means dividing by 3. 27 divided by 3 is 9.

beats.say: 27 divided by 3 is 9. That is the middle sister's age.
The youngest is 2 years younger than the middle one. 9 minus 2 is 7.
So the youngest sister is 7 years old.

board.text: The youngest sister is 7 years old

beats.say: Check: the oldest is 9 plus 2, which is 11. And 7 plus 9 plus 11 is 27. It fits.
Careful: 9 is the middle sister and 11 is the oldest. The question wants the youngest.
When ages are equally spaced, the middle one is the total divided by how many there are.
Five years ago a family had 4 members with an average age of 19. Since then a baby was born. Today the 5 members have an average age of 20. How old is the baby?

board.text: Today: 5 members (a new baby), average age 20

beats.say: An average hides a total. An average of 19 for 4 people means their ages added up to 4 times 19, which is 76.
Those same 4 people are each 5 years older today. How much bigger is their total now?

ask.ifNot: Each of the 4 people grew 5 years older. That is 5, four times over: 4 times 5.

beats.say: 4 times 5 is 20. So today those four add up to 76 plus 20, which is 96.
Now the whole family today: 5 members with an average of 20. Their total is 5 times 20, which is 100.
The only difference between those two totals is the baby. 100 minus 96 is 4.
So the baby is 4 years old.
The trap is to compare 100 with 76 straight away. That forgets that the four older members have each grown 5 years.
So turn averages into totals. Then remember that everyone grows older as time passes.
The ages of a father, a mother and their son add up to 75. The son is 3. What did the family's ages add up to five years ago?

board.text: Father + mother + son = 75 years. The son is 3.
Five years ago, the family's ages added up to ?

beats.say: Five years ago. The son is only 3 now. So where was he five years ago?

ask.ifNot: He is 3 now, so he was born 3 years ago. Five years ago is before that. He was not in the family yet.

beats.say: Not born yet! That is the trap in this question. Five years ago the family was only the father and the mother.
So take the son out. The parents add up to 75 minus 3, which is 72 now.
Five years ago the father was 5 years younger, and the mother was 5 years younger. 5 plus 5 is 10 years less.
72 minus 10 is 62. So five years ago the family's ages added up to 62 years.
If we had taken 5 years off all three people, we would have counted a boy who was not there yet.
So when you go back in time, check that each person had been born.
When Meera was born, her mother was 26. Today her mother is exactly 3 times as old as Meera. How old is her mother today?

board.text: When Meera was born, her mother was 26
Today her mother is 3 times as old. Mother = ?

beats.say: When Meera was 0, her mother was 26. So her mother is 26 years older than her. And that gap never changes.
Today the mother is 3 times as old. So Meera is 1 block and her mother is 3 blocks. The 2 extra blocks are the gap.
The 2 extra blocks make 26 years. So how big is 1 block?

ask.ifNot: 2 blocks are 26 years. One block is half of that: 26 divided by 2.

beats.say: 26 divided by 2 is 13. One block is 13, and that is Meera's age today.
Her mother is 3 blocks. 3 times 13 is 39. So her mother is 39 today.

board.text: Her mother is 39 years old today

beats.say: Check: 39 minus 13 is 26. The gap is right, and 39 is 3 times 13.
Mind the traps. 26 is the gap, not Meera's age, so 26 times 3 does not work. And 13 is Meera, not her mother.
So use the gap that never changes, together with the blocks.
Anu and Bela are 20 together. Bela and Charu are 26 together. Anu and Charu are 24 together. How old is Charu?
Look at the three sums. Each girl appears in exactly two of them.
So if we add all three sums together, what do we get?

ask.ifNot: Count the names. Anu is in two of the sums. Bela is in two. Charu is in two. So every girl is counted twice.

beats.say: 20 plus 26 plus 24 is 70. That is every girl counted twice.
So halve it. 70 divided by 2 is 35. The three girls together are 35 years.
Now the neat part. Anu and Bela together are 20. Take them away from 35, and only Charu is left.
35 minus 20 is 15. So Charu is 15 years old.
Check: Anu is 35 minus 26, which is 9. And Anu plus Charu is 9 plus 15, which is 24. It fits.
When everyone appears twice, add everything and halve. Then take away the pair you do not need.
A father is 40. His three children are 4, 6 and 8. After how many years will the father's age equal the sum of his children's ages?

board.text: Father is 40. His children are 4, 6 and 8.
After ? years: father = sum of the children

beats.say: Today the children add up to 4 plus 6 plus 8, which is 18. The father is 40. So he is ahead by 40 minus 18, which is 22.
Now watch one year go by. The father gains 1 year. But there are three children, and each gains 1. So the children's sum gains 3.
So each year, by how much does the gap close?

ask.ifNot: The children's sum goes up by 3, but the father also goes up by 1. The children catch up by 3 minus 1.

beats.say: 3 minus 1 is 2. The gap closes by 2 every year. This is the trap: not by 3, because the father keeps growing older too.
The gap is 22, and it closes by 2 a year. 22 divided by 2 is 11.
So it happens after 11 years.
Check: in 11 years the father is 51. The children are 15, 17 and 19, and they add up to 51 too.
So find the gap, find how fast it closes each year, and divide.
A mother was 28 when her twin daughters were born. Today the mother and the two twins add up to 64. How old is each twin?

board.text: Mother was 28 when her twins were born
Today: mother + twin + twin = 64. Each twin = ?

beats.say: On the day the twins were born, they were both 0. So the three ages added up to just 28.
Today the total is 64. So it has grown by 64 minus 28, which is 36.
Each year that passes, how much does the total of the three ages grow?

ask.ifNot: Three people each have a birthday: the mother and both twins. So the total goes up by 3 every year.

beats.say: By 3 each year. The trap is to forget the mother. She grows older too!
The total grew by 36, at 3 a year. 36 divided by 3 is 12. So 12 years have passed.
12 years since they were born. So each twin is 12 years old.
Check: the mother is 28 plus 12, which is 40. And 40 plus 12 plus 12 is 64. It fits.
So count how many people are growing older. The total grows by that many every year.
A father's age and his son's age use the same two digits, swapped round. The father is 27 years older. The son is a teenager, 13 to 19. How old is the father?

board.text: Father's and son's ages: same 2 digits, swapped
Father is 27 years older. Son is 13 to 19.

beats.say: The son is a teenager, so there are only a few ages to test. For each one, swap the digits to get the father's age, then check the gap of 27.
Start with 13. Swap the digits and we get 31. The gap is 31 minus 13, which is 18. Too small.
Next, the son is 14. Swap the digits. How old is the father?

ask.ifNot: 14 is written with a 1 and a 4. Swap them round and we get 41.

beats.say: 41 minus 14 is 27. That is exactly the gap we want!
Should we keep going? Try 15 and 51: they are 36 apart. Each year older for the son makes the gap bigger. So 14 is the only one.
So the son is 14 and the father is 41 years old.
Other pairs, like 25 and 52, are also 27 apart. But a son of 25 is not a teenager. Every clue must fit.
When only a few ages are possible, test them one by one against every clue.
Asha is 8. She tells her older sister Bina: when I am as old as you are now, you will be 20. How old is Bina now?

board.text: When Asha is as old as Bina is now, Bina will be 20

beats.say: Let us untangle Asha's sentence. Asha needs some years to reach Bina's age. In those very same years, Bina grows too, and reaches 20.
So there are two equal steps. One from 8 up to Bina's age now. And one from Bina's age now up to 20.
The two equal steps together go from 8 to 20. How long are the two steps together?

ask.ifNot: From 8 up to 20: take 8 away from 20.

beats.say: 20 minus 8 is 12. That is two steps. So one step is 12 divided by 2, which is 6 years.
Bina's age is one step above Asha's 8. 8 plus 6 is 14. So Bina is 14 now.
Check: in 6 years Asha will be 14, which is Bina's age now. And Bina will be 14 plus 6, which is 20. Just as Asha said.
The trap is to stop at 12. That is two steps, not Bina's age. Bina is exactly halfway between 8 and 20.
So the gap between two sisters stays the same. Here it fits twice between 8 and 20.
Ravi's age this year is a multiple of 3. Last year it was a multiple of 4. Next year it will be a multiple of 5. He is under 60. How old is he?

board.text: This year: a multiple of 3. Last year: a multiple of 4.
Next year: a multiple of 5. Under 60. Ravi = ?

beats.say: Three clues, and all must be true together. Let us start with the easiest one to spot: next year's age is a multiple of 5.
Multiples of 5 end in 0 or 5. So what digit does this year's age end in?

ask.ifNot: This year is 1 less than next year. 1 less than a number ending in 0 ends in 9. 1 less than a number ending in 5 ends in 4.

beats.say: So this year's age ends in 9 or 4. Which of those, under 60, are multiples of 3? They are 9, 24, 39 and 54.
Now the last clue. Take 1 away from each to get last year's age: 8, 23, 38 and 53.
Which of those is a multiple of 4?

ask.ifNot: 4 times 2 is 8. None of the others is in the 4 times table.

beats.say: Only 8 works. So last year Ravi was 8, and this year he is 9.

board.text: Ravi is 9 years old this year

beats.say: Check all three clues. 9 is 3 times 3. Last year's 8 is 4 times 2. Next year's 10 is 5 times 2. All of them fit.
Look at 21. It is a multiple of 3, and last year's 20 is a multiple of 4. Tempting! But next year's 22 is not a multiple of 5. Every clue must fit.

board.text: 21: last year 20 fits, next year 22 does not

beats.say: With several clues, use one to make a short list, then test the list against the others.
Ritu and her two brothers are all more than 4 years old. Five years from now their ages will add up to 50. What did they add up to 2 years ago?

board.text: Ritu and her 2 brothers: three children
In 5 years their ages will add up to 50
What did they add up to 2 years ago?

beats.say: We are given a sum in the future and asked for a sum in the past. And there are three children, so every year counts three times.
From 5 years ahead, back to 2 years ago. How many years back is that altogether?

ask.ifNot: First 5 years back to today, then 2 more years back. So 5 plus 2.

beats.say: 5 plus 2 is 7 years back.
Each of the three children was 7 years younger. So the sum was smaller by 3 times 7, which is 21. The trap is to take 7 off only once.
50 minus 21 is 29. So two years ago their ages added up to 29 years.
Check in two steps. Back to today: take off 3 times 5, which is 15, leaving 35. Back 2 more years: take off 3 times 2, which is 6, leaving 29.
And why are we told they are all more than 4 years old? So that we know all three were already born 2 years ago.
So when a sum of ages moves in time, multiply the years by the number of people.
A mother is 5 times as old as her daughter. In 6 years their ages will add up to 60. How old is the daughter now?

board.text: A mother is 5 times as old as her daughter
In 6 years their ages will add up to 60

beats.say: One clue is about today: 5 times as old. The other is about 6 years from now: the sum of 60. We must bring them to the same time.
In 6 years they add up to 60. So what do they add up to today?

ask.ifNot: Both of them will be 6 years older. So today's sum is smaller by 6 for the mother, and by 6 again for the daughter.

beats.say: 60, minus 6, minus 6, is 48. Two people, so the 6 comes off twice. That is the trap here.
Today the daughter is 1 block and the mother is 5 blocks. That is 6 blocks.
6 blocks make 48. 48 divided by 6 is 8. The daughter is one block, so she is 8.

board.text: The daughter is 8 years old now

beats.say: Check: the mother is 5 times 8, which is 40. In 6 years they are 14 and 46, and 14 plus 46 is 60.
So bring the sum to the same time as the other clue. Then use blocks.
The ages of two cousins multiply to give 84. The older one is 5 years older. What do their two ages add up to?

board.text: Two cousins: their ages multiply to give 84
The older is 5 years older. Ages add up to ?

beats.say: We need two numbers that multiply to 84. Let us list the pairs, starting small.
We want the pair that is 5 apart. Which one is it?

ask.ifNot: Find the gap in each pair. 4 and 21 are much too far apart. 14 minus 6 is 8. But 12 minus 7 is 5.

beats.say: 12 minus 7 is 5, and 7 times 12 is 84. So the cousins are 7 and 12.
Now read the question again. It does not ask for either age. It asks what the two ages add up to.
7 plus 12 is 19. So their ages add up to 19.
Pairs like 6 and 14 also multiply to 84, but they are 8 apart, not 5. Both clues must fit.
So list the pairs that multiply to the number, then pick the pair with the right gap.
Kabir's age in months is the same number as his grandfather's age in years. Their ages add up to 78 years. How old is Kabir?

board.text: Kabir's age in months = grandfather's age in years
Their ages add up to 78 years. Kabir = ?

beats.say: A strange clue! Let us try it out. If Kabir were 1 year old, he would be 12 months old. So his grandfather would be 12 years old.
So the grandfather's age is always how many times Kabir's age?

ask.ifNot: Every year of Kabir's age is 12 months. So the number of months is 12 times the number of years.

beats.say: So Kabir is 1 block and his grandfather is 12 blocks. Together that is 13 blocks.
13 blocks make 78 years. 13 times 6 is 78, so one block is 6.
Kabir is one block. So Kabir is 6 years old.
Check: 6 years is 6 times 12, which is 72 months. So his grandfather is 72 years old. And 6 plus 72 is 78.
Careful: 72 is the grandfather's age, and 12 is only the number of months in a year. The question asks for Kabir.
So change both ages to the same unit, see how many times one is of the other, then use blocks.
Tara's age and her uncle's age are in the ratio 2 to 5. Six years ago they were in the ratio 1 to 4. How old is her uncle now?

board.text: Six years ago it was 1 : 4. Uncle now = ?

beats.say: Careful: the 2 and the 5 are not ages. They are parts. So we cannot just take 6 away from them. We need real ages.
Real ages in the ratio 2 to 5 come from multiplying both by the same number. Both must be more than 6, so start at 8 and 20. Then 10 and 25, 12 and 30, 14 and 35.
Take 6 years off each pair. We get 2 and 14, 4 and 19, 6 and 24, 8 and 29.

board.text: 6 years ago: 2 and 14, 4 and 19, 6 and 24, 8 and 29

beats.say: Six years ago the ratio was 1 to 4. So the uncle was 4 times Tara's age. Which pair fits?

ask.ifNot: Multiply the smaller number by 4 and see if you get the bigger one. Only 4 times 6 gives its partner, 24.

beats.say: 4 times 6 is 24. So six years ago Tara was 6 and her uncle was 24.
Come back to today. Tara is 6 plus 6, which is 12. Her uncle is 24 plus 6, which is 30.
So her uncle is 30 years old now.

board.text: Her uncle is 30 years old now

beats.say: Check today's ratio. Divide 12 and 30 by 6 and we get 2 and 5. Yes, 2 to 5.
So list real ages that fit one clue, then test them against the other clue.
Sarika was born in 2006 and Surya was born in 2013. In which year will Sarika be twice the age of Surya?

board.text: Sarika was born in 2006. Surya was born in 2013.
In which year is Sarika twice as old as Surya?

beats.say: First, how much older is Sarika? 2013 minus 2006 is 7. Sarika is 7 years older, and she always will be.
When Sarika is twice Surya's age, Surya is 1 block and Sarika is 2 blocks. Sarika's extra block is the gap.
The gap is 7 years. So how old is Surya when Sarika is twice his age?

ask.ifNot: The extra block is the gap, which is 7. Surya's block is the same size. So Surya is 7.

beats.say: Surya is 7, and Sarika is 7 plus 7, which is 14. And 14 is twice 7.
Now, in which year is Surya 7 years old? He was born in 2013, so add 7. 2013 plus 7 is 2020.
So the year is 2020.
Check with Sarika. 2020 minus 2006 is 14. So in 2020 she is 14 and Surya is 7. Exactly twice.
What about 2019, one year earlier? Then they would be 13 and 6, and twice 6 is 12, not 13. So only 2020 works.
The gap between two ages never changes. When one is double the other, the younger one's age equals the gap.
6 years ago, the ages of a husband and wife added up to 48. Now the husband, wife and son add up to 63. What will the son's age be, 6 years hence?
Three different times are mixed up here: 6 years ago, now, and 6 years from now. The word hence means from now. Let us bring everything to now first.
6 years ago the husband and wife added up to 48. What do the two of them add up to now?

ask.ifNot: The husband is 6 years older now, and the wife is 6 years older too. So add 6 twice.

beats.say: 48, plus 6 for the husband, plus 6 for the wife. That is 60. This is the trap: two people, so we add 6 twice.
Now all three add up to 63. Take away the parents' 60 and the son is left. 63 minus 60 is 3. The son is 3 years old now.
Is 3 our answer?

ask.ifNot: Read the last line again. It asks for the son's age 6 years from now, not his age today.

beats.say: 6 years from now he will be 3 plus 6, which is 9. So the son will be 9 years old.

board.text: The son will be 9 years old

beats.say: So bring every sum to the same time first. And when time moves, add the years once for each person.
Nikhil is 39 and Diya is 32. We want the sum of their ages, but after 6 years.
The word after means we go forward in time, so ages go up. After 6 years Nikhil will be 39 plus 6, which is 45.
Now Diya. What do we do with Diya's age?

ask.ifNot: Time passes for everybody. Diya also grows 6 years older, so we add 6 to 32 as well.

beats.say: Diya grows older as well. 32 plus 6 is 38.
Sum means add. So add the two new ages: 45 plus 38 makes 83.
So after 6 years, their ages will add up to 83.
Here is a quick check. Today they add up to 71. Each of them gains 6 years, so we add 6 twice. We reach 83 again.
Remember the trap: adding the years only once. Two people grow older, so the sum grows twice as much.
Vivek is 30 and Meera is 24. We want the sum of their ages, but after 4 years.
The word after means we go forward in time, so ages go up. After 4 years Vivek will be 30 plus 4, which is 34.
Now Meera. What do we do with Meera's age?

ask.ifNot: Time passes for everybody. Meera also grows 4 years older, so we add 4 to 24 as well.

beats.say: Meera grows older as well. 24 plus 4 is 28.
Now we add the two new ages. 34 plus 28 is 62.
So after 4 years, their ages will add up to 62.
Here is a quick check. Today they add up to 54. Each of them gains 4 years, so we add 4 twice. We reach 62 again.
Remember the trap: adding the years only once. Two people grow older, so the sum grows twice as much.
Two ages today: 50 for Karan and 20 for Ananya. The question takes us back 7 years and asks for the gap between them.
The word ago means we go back in time, so both ages get smaller. 7 years ago Karan was 50 minus 7, which is 43.
Ananya was 7 years younger too. 20 minus 7 is 13.
So back then they were 43 and 13. What is the gap between those two ages?

ask.ifNot: For a gap, take the smaller age away from the bigger one: 43 minus 13.

beats.say: 43 minus 13 is 30. The difference 7 years ago was 30 years.
Now look at today's ages. 50 minus 20 is also 30. The very same gap!
That is no accident. Both of them grew older by the same 7 years, so the gap between them did not change.
So remember: the gap between two people's ages stays the same, in the past, today and for ever. Here it is 30.
Two ages today: 10 for Isha and 25 for Siddharth. The question jumps 10 years ahead and asks what the ages add up to then.
The word after means we go forward in time, so ages go up. After 10 years Isha will be 10 plus 10, which is 20.
Now Siddharth. What do we do with Siddharth's age?

ask.ifNot: Time passes for everybody. Siddharth also grows 10 years older, so we add 10 to 25 as well.

beats.say: Siddharth grows older as well. 25 plus 10 is 35.
Sum means add. So add the two new ages: 20 plus 35 makes 55.
So after 10 years, their ages will add up to 55.
Here is a quick check. Today they add up to 35. Each of them gains 10 years, so we add 10 twice. We reach 55 again.
Remember the trap: adding the years only once. Two people grow older, so the sum grows twice as much.
Two ages today: 35 for Sahil and 12 for Ananya. The question jumps 3 years ahead and asks what the ages add up to then.
The word after means we go forward in time, so ages go up. After 3 years Sahil will be 35 plus 3, which is 38.
Now Ananya. What do we do with Ananya's age?

ask.ifNot: Time passes for everybody. Ananya also grows 3 years older, so we add 3 to 12 as well.

beats.say: Ananya grows older as well. 12 plus 3 is 15.
Sum means add. So add the two new ages: 38 plus 15 makes 53.
So after 3 years, their ages will add up to 53.
Here is a quick check. Today they add up to 47. Each of them gains 3 years, so we add 3 twice. We reach 53 again.
So when time passes, everyone in the sum grows older. Two people means the years are added twice.
Two ages today: 30 for Karan and 32 for Ananya. The question jumps 8 years ahead and asks what the ages add up to then.
The word after means we go forward in time, so ages go up. After 8 years Karan will be 30 plus 8, which is 38.
Now Ananya. What do we do with Ananya's age?

ask.ifNot: Time passes for everybody. Ananya also grows 8 years older, so we add 8 to 32 as well.

beats.say: Ananya grows older as well. 32 plus 8 is 40.
Now we add the two new ages. 38 plus 40 is 78.
So after 8 years, their ages will add up to 78.
Here is a quick check. Today they add up to 62. Each of them gains 8 years, so we add 8 twice. We reach 78 again.
So when time passes, everyone in the sum grows older. Two people means the years are added twice.
Siddharth is 33 and Kavya is 21. We want the difference in their ages, but 7 years ago.
The word ago means we go back in time, so both ages get smaller. 7 years ago Siddharth was 33 minus 7, which is 26.
Kavya was 7 years younger too. 21 minus 7 is 14.
So back then they were 26 and 14. What is the gap between those two ages?

ask.ifNot: For a gap, take the smaller age away from the bigger one: 26 minus 14.

beats.say: 26 minus 14 is 12. The difference 7 years ago was 12 years.
Now look at today's ages. 33 minus 21 is also 12. The very same gap!
Here is why. Every birthday adds 1 year to both of them, so the gap between two ages never changes.
So remember: the gap between two people's ages stays the same, in the past, today and for ever. Here it is 12.
Two ages today: 31 for Aarav and 26 for Neha. The question takes us back 7 years and asks for the gap between them.
The word ago means we go back in time, so both ages get smaller. 7 years ago Aarav was 31 minus 7, which is 24.
Neha was 7 years younger too. 26 minus 7 is 19.
So back then they were 24 and 19. What is the gap between those two ages?

ask.ifNot: For a gap, take the smaller age away from the bigger one: 24 minus 19.

beats.say: 24 minus 19 is 5. The difference 7 years ago was 5 years.
Now look at today's ages. 31 minus 26 is also 5. The very same gap!
That is no accident. Both of them grew older by the same 7 years, so the gap between them did not change.
Next time you can go straight there. The difference in ages never changes, so just subtract today's ages. The answer is 5.
Tara is 15 and Vivek is 31. We want the sum of their ages, but after 5 years.
The word after means we go forward in time, so ages go up. After 5 years Tara will be 15 plus 5, which is 20.
Now Vivek. What do we do with Vivek's age?

ask.ifNot: Time passes for everybody. Vivek also grows 5 years older, so we add 5 to 31 as well.

beats.say: Vivek grows older as well. 31 plus 5 is 36.
Now we add the two new ages. 20 plus 36 is 56.
So after 5 years, their ages will add up to 56.
Here is a quick check. Today they add up to 46. Each of them gains 5 years, so we add 5 twice. We reach 56 again.
So when time passes, everyone in the sum grows older. Two people means the years are added twice.
